clue.text: Left its reins flapping

indicators.note: reins flapping loose are in disorder, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A rider has let go and the reins are flapping about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a past tense (the reins were abandoned), but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is the heraldic Latin word for the left-hand side.

clue.text: One may train each day before and after work

definitions.text: One may train each day before and after work

parts.words: One may train each day before and after work
parts.note: the surface suggests someone exercising twice a day, but 'train' means travel by rail to and from the job

explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' reads as a verb of fitness training; it is really taking the train.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily rail traveller going to and from the office is the classic picture of this person.

clue.text: Separate line of descent

definitions.meaning: to filter or sieve liquid from solids, as with a colander
a breed, lineage or variety descended from common stock

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to sieve apart and a particular hereditary stock or lineage.

clue.text: Musical instruments belonging to a 'Twelfth Night' character

definitions.meaning: stringed instruments a little larger than violins
Viola is the heroine of Shakespeare's play, and the possessive of her name gives the same letters

explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the alto string instrument, and also the possessive of Shakespeare's shipwrecked heroine's name.

clue.text: Destroyer worried boat user

indicators.note: worried in the sense of shaken about or harried, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone using a boat is anxious about a warship nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyer' tempts as a warship beside the boat, but it means a wrecker.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately wrecks or damages things, so is a person who destroys.

clue.text: Small pill the Parisian found in shower

indicators.note: the French article is discovered sitting within the word for a downpour

parts.note: to pelt is to rain heavily, a pelting shower
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone finds a tiny tablet lying in the shower.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet is a small compressed ball, such as a tablet of medicine.

clue.text: Leading at home with assurance

parts.note: being in means being at home
front means boldness or brazen self-confidence

explanation.surface: A team is winning comfortably on its own ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ahead in a race or contest means being the leader.

clue.text: Cast having fish after starter of figs

indicators.note: the fish comes after the first letter
the starter of a word is its opening letter, as a starter opens a meal

parts.note: the ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: A meal of fish served after a fig starter.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling something is to throw or hurl it, synonymous with casting it.

clue.text: Military unit ordered to install equipment

indicators.note: installing something puts it in place within, so the gear goes inside the command word

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning commanded
a rig is a set of equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: Soldiers have been told to set up their gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like an anagram signal; it is BADE, holding RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is an army formation made up of several battalions.

clue.text: Titled man, right individual to be accepted by club

indicators.note: being accepted by something means being taken in, so these letters go inside the club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sports such as cricket
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A decent person is admitted into a members' club.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British title, ranking below a baron, and is styled Sir.

clue.text: Turn of phrase fool almost used facing Bond's boss

indicators.note: the shortened word sits facing, that is in front of, the next piece
almost the whole word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: an idiot is a fool
M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A silly remark is made in front of James Bond's spymaster.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression whose meaning is not literal, a turn of phrase.

clue.text: Hoax victim taken from pool, frail, shivering

indicators.note: shivering means trembling, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A weak swimmer is pulled shivering from a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fooled by a prank on the first of April is the classic hoax victim.

clue.text: Gent in best hotel resolved to live more frugally

indicators.note: resolved in the sense of broken down and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gentleman staying at the finest hotel decides to cut his spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' reads as 'decided', but it signals the letters being re-sorted.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to economise, as if pulling a belt in a notch on less food.

clue.text: Keep back, quietly avoiding jam

indicators.note: avoiding the letter means it is left out of the word

parts.note: preserve is jam or conserve
P is the music abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Someone holds back from eating jam, keeping quiet about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something is to set it aside or hold it back for later.

clue.text: Conventional poker hand

definitions.meaning: a run of five cards in consecutive order

explanation.definitionFit: The word means orthodox or square, and also names a five-card sequence in poker.

clue.text: Beginning to egg on worker showing class

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket
an ant is the standard crossword worker, from the worker ant

explanation.surface: Someone starting to urge on a labourer who shows real quality.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side, so 'on' gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Being elegant means having style and refinement, which is having class.

clue.text: Opening of these centres is what interests a culture vulture

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: hearts are centres, as in the heart of the city

explanation.surface: The opening of new arts centres excites a lover of culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' suggests a ribbon-cutting ceremony; it just takes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A culture vulture is an avid consumer of painting, music, theatre and literature.

clue.text: Tea eagerly ordered round middle of afternoon

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round, enclosing, the central letter
ordered as in put into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
the middle of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Someone keenly orders a cuppa in the mid-afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' makes EARLGEY from 'eagerly'; 'round' puts it around R, the fifth letter of 'afternoon'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a popular black tea flavoured with bergamot oil.

clue.text: Check into earlier vessel

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes into the other word

parts.note: sooner means earlier
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Someone checks onto a ship before the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing ship with two or more masts, fore-and-aft rigged.

clue.text: Factors, perhaps abroad, restricting daughter much in need of money

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the shuffled letters hold the single letter inside
abroad in the old sense of widely scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Agents working overseas keep their daughter on a tight budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Factors' and 'perhaps' together are the fodder; their shuffled letters go round D.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being short of funds, as if bound tight by lack of money.

clue.text: Present doctor turned up in case

indicators.note: the turned letters sit in the middle of the other word

parts.note: a suit is a legal case, a lawsuit

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor turns up at court to present a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To submit evidence or a proposal is to present or put it forward.

clue.text: Poor mate shot

parts.note: pal means mate or friend
a try, as in having a shot at something

explanation.surface: A friend's attempt was not up to much.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means meagre or contemptibly small, so poor in quality or amount.

clue.text: Plump domestic, not quite sound

parts.note: fat means plump

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so it loses its last letter

parts.note: home as an adjective means domestic, as in home affairs

explanation.surface: A chubby servant is not entirely of sound mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' looks like a noun for a servant; it is the adjective HOME. 'Sound' is the verb, as in sounding the depth.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound water is to measure its depth, and a nautical depth unit gives the verb with that sense.

clue.text: Intended to help me inside

indicators.note: the personal pronoun goes inside the helping word

parts.note: to aid is to help

explanation.surface: Someone meant to come to my assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimed, as in aimed to do something, means meant or intended.

clue.text: Excellent food fish –- a tin unexpectedly produced

parts.note: brill is a flatfish eaten as food, related to turbot

indicators.note: turning out unexpectedly means in an unforeseen order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fish surprisingly comes out of a tin and tastes excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent' and 'food fish' both tempt as the fish's description; the definition is the first word alone, and 'unexpectedly' signals the rearrangement of 'a tin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant is a strong word of praise, meaning outstanding or superb.

clue.text: Old boy with beaker returned for soup

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a mug is a drinking beaker

explanation.surface: A former pupil hands back his cup to be filled with soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumbo is a thick stew-like soup from Louisiana, thickened with okra.

clue.text: Trendy? That girl must be with it to succeed

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
her refers to that girl

explanation.surface: A fashionable girl needs to be with it to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' means to follow as heir, not to triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone is to take over their title or estate as heir.

clue.text: Late series of deliveries? Exactly

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or delivered, by one bowler
due means exactly, as in due north

explanation.surface: A batch of parcels has arrived late, precisely as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls from one bowler, each called a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has not arrived by the time expected, so it is late.
